title: Tab lens slides twice after every phone tab change (snaps back to the old tab, then springs again)
reference_evidence: Lonora-Desktop-37.html:3433-3437 setupNav(prev): after a re-render the lens is put back at lensPos (where the pager left it, already on the new tab, set in paintTabs line 4274 `lensPos={x,w}`) and then placeLens(true) has nothing left to move. DESIGN_TREE_37.md:273/294: the lens follows the progress and then stops; it slides once (0.42 spring, width 0.32). Measured in the reference: going from updates to tasks, the lens moves 195→108 and stays at 108.
app_evidence: pager.ts finish() (around lines 248-262) calls flushSync(commit(route)) and then placeLens(s.nav,false). The router has not yet moved `button.active`, so lens.ts placeLens puts the lens back on the OLD tab with no transition. When React then renders the new active tab, the [section] effect in FloatingTabBar.tsx:52-66 calls placeLens(nav,true), which plays the CSS spring a second time. Frame trace in scripts/phone/s6.mjs: on a tap from updates to tasks the pager carries the lens 195→108 by t=1643ms, at t=1731 it is back at 195 with the route now on tasks, then it springs 195→104 (overshoot) →108. The same happens on tasks→updates (195, then 108, then 199, then 195) and updates→settings (20, then 195, then 13, then 20). Over 10 taps in s5.mjs, 8 showed backward jumps of 40px or more in a single frame.
owner_sees: On every tab change on the phone (tap, swipe or lens drag), the lens arrives under the new tab, jumps back under the tab it came from, and slides over a second time with a bounce. The tab bar flickers, where the reference has one smooth slide.
fix_plan: In pager.ts finish() and reset(), place the lens from the target's own rect (lensRect(s.toBtn) on commit, lensRect(s.fromBtn) on reset) instead of calling placeLens(nav), which reads the stale `.active`. Keep a module-level `lensPos` as the reference does. In FloatingTabBar.tsx, the [section] effect should start the lens at that remembered lensPos and only then call placeLens(nav,true), as setupNav(prev) does, so nothing moves when the lens is already in place. Alternatively, skip the animated placement when the lens transform already equals the active tab's rect. Add a Playwright check in tests/web that samples the lens left edge every frame after a tab tap and asserts it never moves away from the target.
verifier_note: Simplest fix: in finish() and reset(), place the lens from the target button's rect (lensRect(s.toBtn) on commit, lensRect(s.fromBtn) on reset). Alternatively drop the placeLens call in finish() and let the [section] effect place it with animate=false when the lens is already at the target. Keep the animated call only for taps that did not go through the pager. Check the lens-drag release path (onLensRelease) and foldNav, which also use placeLens. No money-safety risk. Overlaps nothing in this batch.
